days.title: Northeastern Lakes and Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Lac de Joux
stops.detail: The northeastern part of the valley is occupied by Lac de Joux and Lac Brenet.

stops.name: Lac Brenet
stops.detail: Today, Lac de Joux and Lac Brenet serve as storage reservoirs for the Vallorbe power station.

stops.name: Le Pont
stops.detail: The most important towns are Le Sentier and Le Brassus (municipality of Le Chenit) as well as Le Pont (municipality of L’Abbaye) on the northeastern shore of Lac de Joux.

stops.name: Dent de Vaulion
stops.detail: The northeastern end of the valley is characterized by the Dent de Vaulion and the hill chain of the Col du Mont d’Orzeires, which were moved to their current position by a strike-slip fault in the system of the Jura chains.

days.title: Southern Valley Towns and Ridges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Le Sentier
stops.detail: In Le Sentier, there is a large sports center, a watch museum, and an art gallery.

stops.name: Mont-Tendre-Kette
stops.detail: The valley forms a syncline, flanked to the southeast by the folds (anticlines) of the Mont Tendre chain and to the northwest by those of the Risoux chain.
